Native USB · SPI: 2× 74HC595, MCP4821 DAC, 23LC1024 SRAM · VSYS = 5 V / 3.3 V (J4) · ZIF-28 · purple = changed in Rev H. Same-name labels are joined.

GND/VCC are switched per size (see ZIF-28 switching, bottom)
SW1: VSYS → VCC_SKT. OFF to insert/remove. C2/C3 by Q6/Q7.
SW1 also removes VBOOST, so VPP collapses to 0 V.
VPP generator: MIC2288 boost → DAC → op-amp → pass transistor (0 … 17.4 V)

U6B unused: pin 5 → GND, pin 6 → pin 7. U6 pin 8 = VBOOST, pin 4 = GND.

g.text: SPI0 bus (mode 0): who is selected by what
The 595 chain sees every SPI byte, but its outputs move only when PA7 is
pulsed, so firmware sends both 595 bytes (U9 first) right before each latch.
R13 pulls DAC_OUT to 0 V whenever U3 is in shutdown or unwritten, so VPP
starts at 0 V; firmware writes the idle code (1176 @5 V, 776 @3.3 V) at boot.
Max SCK 12 MHz at 5 V; at 3.3 V keep SCK ≤ 8 MHz for the 74HC595.
1. Net labels with the same name are connected. ZIF pin roles come from the device pinout spreadsheet.
2. Port-pin names only: take SPDIP/SSOP pin numbers from the AVR DU datasheet (DS40002576, §2.4).
3. SPI0: PA4 MOSI, PA5 MISO, PA6 SCK; PA7 = 595 latch (GPIO; set SPI0 CTRLB.SSD). No I2C in this revision.
4. Each SPI device has its own select (table, bottom left); /CS pull-ups keep U3 and U7 deselected at reset.
5. No crystal: PA0/PA1 and PF0/PF1 are used as GPIO. Confirm crystal-less USB in the datasheet.
6. C14 (VUSB) value and any D+/D− series resistors: per the datasheet's USB section.
7. MCP4821 internal reference: trim the DAC code against the PD1 ADC readback (internal 2.500 V ref).
8. Check the LM358 loop for oscillation at 5 V and 16.5 V; adjust C10 (470p–4.7n) if needed.
9. U4: VBOOST = 1.24 V × (1 + R34/R35) ≈ 21.0 V. TSOT-23 part has no OVP: 1% resistors, inspect FB before power-up.
10. BOOST_EN (U9 Q3) low or Hi-Z (R36) = boost off: VBOOST ≈ VCC_SKT − 0.4 V, so VPP stays ≤ ~3 V.
11. U7 holds the fuse map (lifts the 2 KB limit). All 19 MCU pins are used; PA3 now reads SDOUT (ZIF15).
12. Schematic-level reference, not a verified board. Breadboard (SPDIP-28) before ordering PCBs.
ZIF pin map derived from Afterburner (ole00)
Logic supply select (new in Rev G): VSYS = 5 V or 3.3 V
SOT-223, 1.2 A, stable with ceramic caps.
C17/C18 values per the LDL1117 datasheet.
from U1's internal USB regulator (USBVREG = 1), as Rev F
tied to VDD; firmware writes SYSCFG.VUSBCTRL.USBVREG = 0
VSYS feeds: U1 VDD (pins 18, 24), U2, U3, U7, J3 pin 2, the R12/R15/R32/R33 pull-ups,
and SW1 → VCC_SKT (ZIF 28 / ZIF 7 via Q6 / Q7, and the U4 boost input). +5V (VBUS after F1) feeds only J4 and U8.
13. Move the J4 shunts only with USB unplugged, and keep both on the same side (silkscreen "5V | 3V3"). Mixed positions put the wrong voltage on VUSB.
14. 3.3 V mode is the datasheet's external-3.3 V power configuration (VDD = VUSB). USB needs VDD ≥ 3.0 V. Check C14 against that configuration.
15. No MCU pin is free for a sense line: firmware measures VDD with the ADC at boot (VDDDIV10 input; confirm the DU has it) and refuses 5 V-only parts at 3.3 V.
16. 3.3 V mode is for low-voltage parts (e.g. ATF16LV8C, ATF22LV10C) and needs Afterburner support for them. GAL16V8/20V8/22V10 and ATF16V8B/22V10C are 5 V only.
17. Firmware changes: U3 at 1× gain (GA bit = 1); VPP = DAC × 8.5; ADC on the 2.500 V reference (R16 68k keeps VPP_SENSE ≤ 2.7 V at maximum VBOOST, below VSYS).
18. Q1 must be a logic-level FET (AO3400, rated at Vgs 2.5 V). In 3.3 V mode U8 also feeds the MIC2288 (≈0.2 A at the 30 mA VPP limit): check U8's temperature.

svg.text: ZIF-28 switching (new in Rev H): U9 second 595, GND and VCC switches, series resistors
R43: U2 Q1 still drives ZIF7 (RA3 for 22V10) but can't
fight Q7 when ZIF7 is the 26CV12's VCC (set Q1 high).
R44: ZIF12 is SCLK for 28-pin, GND (Q4) for 24-pin.
Firmware interlock: one GND and one VCC switch per size; all off at reset. Never Q6 with Q7; never Q4 with a 28-pin chip.
